questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: The two-ray model of a film
questions.learningObjective: Explain how two reflected rays create film interference.
questions.stem: A film 400 nm thick has index 1.5; two-ray path difference in nanometres?
questions.explanation: The second ray travels down and back through the film, so path difference is two n t, giving 1200 nm.
questions.hint: Double the product of index and thickness.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Phase change on reflection from a denser medium
questions.learningObjective: Explain phase change on reflection from a denser medium.
questions.stem: A graph interpreter checks reflection at an air-glass boundary.

options.text: Reflection from a denser medium adds a half-wavelength phase shift.
Reflection from a denser medium adds no phase shift.
Reflection from a rarer medium adds the shift.
Phase shift equals a full wavelength.
options.misconception: uses full wavelength instead of half

questions.explanation: When light reflects from a medium of higher refractive index, the reflected wave gains a half-wavelength phase shift. This shift changes which thicknesses are bright or dark.
questions.hint: Denser reflector gives half-wave shift.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Thinnest film giving a dark reflection
questions.learningObjective: Explain the thinnest film producing a dark reflection.
questions.stem: Why is the thinnest dark film not simply zero thickness?

answer.exemplar: For a film with one phase reversal, destructive interference first occurs when the round-trip path equals one wavelength, giving thickness lambda over two n.

questions.explanation: Zero thickness gives no film, so the first dark fringe needs a nonzero round trip of one wavelength.
questions.hint: Use the first nonzero dark condition.

provenance.author: bank-team-physics-em
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Thinnest film giving a bright reflection
questions.learningObjective: Explain the thinnest film producing a bright reflection.
questions.stem: At 600 nm and index 1.5, thinnest bright film thickness in nanometres?
questions.explanation: With one phase reversal, first bright occurs at a quarter-wavelength round trip, so thickness is lambda over four n.
questions.hint: Divide wavelength by four times index.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: The two-ray model of a film
questions.learningObjective: Explain how two reflected rays create film interference.
questions.stem: A film 150 nm thick has index 1.8; two-ray path difference in nanometres?
questions.explanation: The second ray travels down and back through the film, so path difference is two n t, giving 540 nm.
questions.hint: Double the product of index and thickness.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Phase change on reflection from a denser medium
questions.learningObjective: Explain phase change on reflection from a denser medium.
questions.stem: A denser boundary is checked for phase shift.

options.text: Reflection from a denser medium adds no phase shift.
Reflection from a denser medium adds a half-wavelength phase shift.
Reflection from a rarer medium adds the shift.
Phase shift equals a full wavelength.
options.misconception: uses full wavelength instead of half

questions.explanation: When light reflects from a medium of higher refractive index, the reflected wave gains a half-wavelength phase shift. This shift changes which thicknesses are bright or dark.
questions.hint: Denser reflector gives half-wave shift.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Thinnest film giving a dark reflection
questions.learningObjective: Explain the thinnest film producing a dark reflection.
questions.stem: What nonzero thickness gives the first dark film?

answer.exemplar: For a film with one phase reversal, destructive interference first occurs when the round-trip path equals one wavelength, giving thickness lambda over two n.

questions.explanation: Zero thickness gives no film, so the first dark fringe needs a nonzero round trip of one wavelength.
questions.hint: Use the first nonzero dark condition.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Thinnest film giving a bright reflection
questions.learningObjective: Explain the thinnest film producing a bright reflection.
questions.stem: At 480 nm and index 1.2, thinnest bright film thickness in nanometres?
questions.explanation: With one phase reversal, first bright occurs at a quarter-wavelength round trip, so thickness is lambda over four n.
questions.hint: Divide wavelength by four times index.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: A film on a denser substrate reverses the conditions
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a denser substrate reverses bright and dark conditions.
questions.stem: For a film on a denser substrate, thinnest dark thickness at 525 nm and index 1.75 in nanometres?
questions.explanation: Changing the substrate changes the phase reversals at boundaries, so bright and dark thickness conditions swap. The film index alone no longer decides.
questions.hint: Use the reversed dark condition.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Index of a wedge film from its fringe spacing
questions.learningObjective: Explain how fringe spacing gives a wedge film index.
questions.stem: Fringe count is converted to wedge film index.

options.text: Index equals fringe spacing divided by wavelength.
Index equals wavelength divided by fringe spacing only.
Index equals fringe count times wavelength divided by twice path length times angle.
Index is independent of fringe spacing.

questions.explanation: Count fringes over a known length and angle, then use n equals N lambda over two L tan theta. This converts spacing into refractive index.
questions.hint: Include fringe count, length, and angle.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Fringe spacing in an air wedge
questions.learningObjective: Explain fringe spacing in an air wedge.
questions.stem: What determines fringe spacing in an air wedge?

answer.exemplar: In an air wedge, successive fringes differ by lambda over two in path, so spacing is lambda over two tan theta.

questions.explanation: The wedge thickness changes linearly, so equal path increments occur at equal distances.
questions.hint: Path changes by lambda over two.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Radius of a Newton's ring
questions.learningObjective: Explain the radius of a Newton's ring.
questions.stem: Eighth dark Newton's ring with 600 nm light and 1 m radius lens; radius in millimetres?
questions.explanation: The air gap thickness grows quadratically with radius, so r squared equals m lambda R for the mth dark ring.
questions.hint: Take square root of m lambda R.
